why_ai: Nurses, technicians and psychiatrists hold, observe and treat people in crisis on locked units around the clock, psychiatrists sign holds and carry liability, and patients held involuntarily did not choose their provider, so trust is 3.
why_clarity: Admissions and per diem rules repeat daily, but whether a patient is stable enough to leave is contested and readmission shows up weeks later.
why_digital: Care starts and ends with a person on a locked unit, and admissions come from local emergency departments, courts and police.

why_ai: Reading notes and assembling necessity evidence automates, but whether a psychiatric day is necessary is a contested judgement signed by a psychiatrist and examined by prosecutors.
why_clarity: Reviews recur every few days for every stay against written criteria, but payers and auditors disagree on what counts as necessity.
why_digital: Notes and criteria in, arguments out on screen, delivered by phone to payer reviewers and as audit files.

why_ai: Drafting review packets from notes is extraction work AI does well; the attending's peer-to-peer argument keeps some human accountability.
why_clarity: Each review gets an approve, cut or deny answer within a day, thousands of times a year, against written payer criteria.
why_digital: Records and portals in, phone reviews out, with each payer's reviewer on a scheduled call.

why_ai: Checking certification dates and documentation against written CMS rules automates, though compliance officers stay accountable at audit.
why_clarity: The IPF documentation rules are explicit and apply to every stay, but audit findings arrive a year or more later.
why_digital: Charts in, deficiency lists and audit files out, all on screen and often handled by remote auditors.

why_ai: The JV runs locked hospitals staffed by licensed clinicians, and the partnership rests on trust between the health system and the operator.
why_clarity: Leakage and occupancy can be counted, but each partnership and market is different and results take years.
why_digital: Beds, staff and buildings are physical and local, sold to a regional health system face to face.

why_ai: Licensed intake clinicians and physicians decide whether a referred patient is medically safe for a unit without a medical floor, a high-stakes call on incomplete packets.
why_clarity: Referrals arrive by the thousand, but medical clearance criteria differ by unit and the outcome is known only days later.
why_digital: Packets arrive by fax and phone from local emergency departments and end in a patient transported to the unit.

why_ai: Technicians and nurses watch, de-escalate and physically restrain patients on the unit, under orders and liability that rest on licensed staff.
why_clarity: Federal rules fix the timing of checks and orders and hours are counted, but preventing an escalation is judgement that varies by staff member.
why_digital: The work is bodies in rooms on a locked unit, observed and handled in person.

why_ai: Physicians and nurses manage dangerous withdrawal in person with controlled medications, and patients choose programmes they trust.
why_clarity: Withdrawal protocols and scores are written down and repeat, but whether the patient stays in treatment is known only after discharge.
why_digital: Patients are treated on site and placed into local or regional programmes.

why_ai: Licensed clinicians treat minors in person with their families, and parents choose a unit they trust with their child.
why_clarity: Each youth's family and school situation differs, and whether treatment worked shows up weeks or months later.
why_digital: Care is delivered on a locked unit and through in-person family work, referred locally.

why_ai: Abstracting measures and validating assessment records against published specifications is rule-bound data work that software performs.
why_clarity: Measure specifications and assessment items are published and every record passes or fails CMS's checks.
why_digital: Records in, submission files out through CMS systems, handled remotely by vendors.

why_ai: Clocks and drafting automate, but a psychiatrist must sign each certification personally and defend it in court.
why_clarity: State statutes define each element and deadline, and a hearing gives a quick, clear outcome.
why_digital: Charts and statutes in, documents out on screen, but hearings are local and often in person on the unit.

why_ai: Clients pay for named analysts' reading of CMS rules, but summarising a published rule is work LLMs already do.
why_clarity: The rule cycle repeats every year and impacts can be checked against the final rule, though each client question differs.
why_digital: Rules and public files in, briefs and models out, sold to national clients remotely.

why_ai: Internal analytics carry no licence, but executives rely on analysts who know the facilities, and the questions are high-stakes under investigation.
why_clarity: Dashboards recur monthly, but strategic questions about length of stay and JVs are one-off and slow to resolve.
why_digital: Records and claims in, dashboards and board papers out, used inside one company.

why_ai: Collecting bed status and routing referrals is software work with no licence attached, though states value a trusted neutral vendor.
why_clarity: Each bed is open or not and each referral is accepted or not, updated many times a day.
why_digital: Bed data in, a live registry out online, sold mostly to state agencies.

why_ai: Detecting risky movement on video is computer vision that keeps improving, while hospitals still need staff to respond in the room.
why_clarity: Alerts are frequent and checkable, but which behaviours predict harm is still argued.
why_digital: Cameras watch physical patients, observers work on screens, and alerts send staff to the bedside.

why_ai: Physical intervention skills are taught and practised in person by certified trainers whose programmes hospitals trust.
why_clarity: Curricula are codified and repeated for every new hire, but whether training reduced restraint is known only over months.
why_digital: Training is hands-on in hospitals, though content and certification records are digital and sold nationally.

why_ai: Clinician reviewers carry some accountability, but assembling and arguing reviews from notes is work AI is starting to do.
why_clarity: Reviews and claims recur by the thousand with quick payer answers.
why_digital: Charts and portals in, reviews and claims out, done remotely for facilities.

why_ai: Chart abstraction against published measure specifications is exactly what document AI replaces.
why_clarity: Specifications are exact and every abstracted case is checkable.
why_digital: Charts in, measure files out, fully remote.

why_ai: Assessors walk units in person and their name on the assessment matters to surveyors, though photo-based detection will help.
why_clarity: The design guide's risk levels are written down, but whether an assessment prevented a suicide attempt is rarely known.
why_digital: The work starts on site in a building, with reports delivered to hospitals and architects in the region.

why_ai: Underwriters judge rare, high-severity risks and brokers sell on relationships, though pricing models automate.
why_clarity: Rating rules exist, but claims and verdicts arrive years after the policy.
why_digital: Applications and loss runs in, quotes out, sold through brokers.

why_ai: Members trust the PSO with privileged event reports, and finding causes in rare events takes judgement.
why_clarity: Event types recur, but root causes are argued and improvements show slowly.
why_digital: Event reports in, analyses out, shared with members remotely.

why_ai: Members trust their association with their data, while tabulating a survey is routine work.
why_clarity: The survey repeats every year on the same fields, but its effect on policy is slow and unmeasured.
why_digital: Member data in, a report out online, sold to members across the country.
